title: spec(ui)+metadata save: judge a flattened view overlay's top-level `options.KIND` with the strict per-kind schema and persist the PARSED body — the door half of objectui#10380
body:
Filing gate ③: a ruled task. Director seat, summon #29 (`session_01EcrTi7s5oDYPHS4Pi7h31d`), executing objectui#10380 batch #223 item 5a, letter A. Maintainer verbatim: 「其他同意」. ⛔ Not a claim. Routing and grading are triage's.

## What
`PUT /api/v1/meta/view` with a flattened list overlay passes the door through `ListViewShapeSchema.extend(flattenedViewOverlayFields()).strip()` (`packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`, the listOverlay member). A top-level `options` bag is **stripped unjudged**: `options.timeline.metaFields` passes, while the same key written directly (`timeline.metaFields`) is refused `unrecognized_keys`. `saveMetaItem` then persists the **original** body verbatim, and objectui's interface page forwards `view.options` into the renderer. So a stored view carries and renders keys the strict schemas refuse, and it renders two ways (the object page does not forward `options`). This was measured by the objectui#10222 dev on the installed spec 17.4.0; the persistence step was read from source.

## Deliverable (ruling A)
- The door judges each `options.KIND` present on a flattened overlay with that kind's strict schema, and refuses an out-of-contract key **by name**, exactly as the direct spelling is refused. `options.map` (the deliberately kept legacy path, pinned in objectui) stays accepted as far as its kind's schema accepts it.
- Persistence stores the **parsed** body, not the request body, so nothing unjudged reaches storage.
- **Stored-row census** before landing: how many stored views carry a top-level `options.*`, and which keys. The result goes on objectui#10380 and in the changeset; rows that fail the new judgement are named with their fix.
- Pins: a direct and an `options`-wrapped out-of-contract key get the same refusal; a legal `options.KIND` round-trips; the persisted body equals the parse result.

## Unblocks
objectui#10380 (`Blocked-by:` this card). objectui then only aligns, so that the same stored view renders the same on the interface page and the object page. objectui#10222 (retiring the `metaFields` reads) does not wait on this card.
